senses.def: to give someone a job, or to pay someone to do a particular task
examples: The company plans to hire 200 new workers this year.
We hired a lawyer to help with the contract.

senses.def: (British) to pay to use something for a short time
examples: We hired a boat for the afternoon.

senses.def: (American) a person who has just been given a job
examples: All new hires must complete safety training.

note: In American English you "rent" a car or apartment; "hire" for these is British. Americans "hire" people.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with a man, boy, or male animal already mentioned
examples: He lost his wallet on the subway.
His sister is a nurse.

senses.def: something that belongs to him
examples: That jacket isn't mine — it's his.
She's a cousin of his.

note: Same form as determiner and pronoun: his car / the car is his.

senses.def: a person who studies or writes about history
examples: Historians still disagree about the causes of the war.
She's an art historian at a museum in Boston.

senses.def: important in history, or likely to be remembered as important
examples: The election was a historic moment for the country.
The two leaders signed a historic peace agreement.

senses.def: old and of historical interest
examples: We walked around the historic district of Charleston.

note: Historic = important in history; historical = connected with the past (historical records). Not interchangeable.

senses.def: connected with the past or with the study of history
examples: The museum has a large collection of historical documents.
She writes historical novels set in the 1800s.

senses.def: that really existed or happened in the past
examples: Was King Arthur a historical figure or just a legend?

note: Compare: a historical novel (set in the past) vs. a historic victory (very important).

senses.def: all the events of the past, or the study of them
examples: She's studying American history in college.
This was the worst storm in the city's history.

senses.def: the past experiences or record of a person or thing
examples: The patient has a history of heart problems.
Check your browser history to find the website.

note: "Make history" = do something important that will be remembered. "That's history" = it no longer matters.

senses.def: to touch someone or something quickly and with force
examples: He hit the ball over the fence.
A truck hit our car from behind.

senses.def: to have a bad effect on someone or something
examples: The town was badly hit by the floods.
Rising prices have hit poor families the hardest.

senses.def: to reach a particular level or point
examples: Temperatures hit 100 degrees yesterday.
Sales hit a record high in December.

senses.tr: hit, çok tutulan şey; darbe, vuruş
senses.def: a very successful song, movie, or show, or an act of hitting
examples: The song was a huge hit in the 1980s.
The ship took a direct hit.

note: Irregular: hit – hit – hit. "Hit it off" = like each other immediately.

senses.def: an activity you do for pleasure in your free time
examples: My hobbies include hiking and photography.
He started gardening as a hobby after he retired.

senses.def: (American) a game played on ice by two teams using sticks to hit a small rubber disk into a goal
examples: My son plays hockey every winter.
Hockey is hugely popular in Canada.

note: In the US, "hockey" means ice hockey; the game on grass is "field hockey". In Britain it is the reverse.

senses.def: to have something in your hands or arms
examples: She was holding a baby in her arms.
Hold the ladder while I climb up.

senses.def: to organize a meeting, event, or election
examples: The meeting will be held on Tuesday.
They hold a festival every summer.

senses.def: to contain a particular amount, or to have a position, title, or opinion
examples: The stadium can hold 50,000 people.
She holds a degree in engineering.

senses.def: the act of holding something, or control over something
examples: Keep a tight hold on the rope.
The company's hold on the market is weakening.

note: Irregular: hold – held – held. "Hold on" = wait. "Put somebody on hold" = make them wait on the phone.

senses.def: an empty space or opening in something solid or in a surface
examples: There's a hole in my sock.
The dog dug a hole in the backyard.

senses.def: a weakness or missing part in an argument, plan, or budget
examples: The lawyer found several holes in the witness's story.
The tax cuts left a hole in the city budget.

note: "Pick holes in something" = find faults in it. Sounds the same as "whole".

senses.def: a day when most people do not work because of a religious or national celebration
examples: Thanksgiving is a national holiday in the US.
Stores are busy during the holidays.

senses.def: (British) a period of time away from work or school, often traveling
examples: They're on holiday in Spain for two weeks.

note: Americans say "vacation" for time off traveling; "the holidays" usually means late December. "On holiday" is British.

senses.def: having an empty space inside
examples: Birds were nesting in a hollow tree.
The walls sounded hollow when I knocked on them.

senses.def: without real value, meaning, or sincerity
examples: His promises turned out to be hollow.
It was a hollow victory because so many lives were lost.

senses.def: a small area that is lower than the land around it
examples: The village sits in a hollow between two hills.

note: "Ring hollow" = sound insincere or untrue.

senses.def: connected with God or religion, and treated with great respect
examples: Jerusalem is a holy city for three major religions.
Ramadan is the holiest month in the Islamic calendar.

senses.def: living a good, religious life
examples: He was considered a holy man by the villagers.

note: "Holy cow!" is an informal expression of surprise.

senses.def: the place where you live, especially with your family
examples: I usually work from home on Fridays.
Thousands of people lost their homes in the earthquake.

senses.def: the town or country you come from, or a place where people who need care live
examples: Italy is home to some of the world's greatest art.
She moved her father into a nursing home.

senses.def: to or at the place where you live
examples: What time did you get home last night?
I'm staying home tonight.

senses.tr: ev, evle ilgili; yerli, ev sahibi (takım)
senses.def: connected with your house, or with your own country or team
examples: Please write your home address.
The home team won by three points.

note: No "to" before home as an adverb: "go home", not "go to home". A frequent error for Turkish speakers.

senses.def: the country where you were born or where your people come from
examples: Many refugees dream of returning to their homeland.
After 30 years abroad, he visited his homeland again.

note: "Homeland security" (US) = protecting the country from terrorism and disasters.

senses.def: having no home, and often living on the streets
examples: The shelter provides beds for homeless families.
He was homeless for two years before he found work.

senses.def: (the homeless) people who have no home
examples: She volunteers at a soup kitchen for the homeless.

senses.def: school work that students do at home
examples: I have a lot of math homework tonight.
Did you finish your homework before dinner?

senses.def: research or preparation you do before an important event
examples: Do your homework before you buy a used car.

note: Uncountable: "a lot of homework", not "homeworks". Say "do homework", not "make homework".

senses.def: always telling the truth and not cheating or stealing
examples: She's an honest person who would never lie to you.
Be honest with me — do you like the dress?

senses.def: said or done sincerely, without hiding the truth
examples: I'd like your honest opinion about my essay.
To be honest, I don't really enjoy parties.

note: The h is silent: "an honest man".

senses.def: the quality of being truthful and not cheating
examples: I appreciate your honesty, even if the news is bad.
Honesty is the most important thing in a relationship.

senses.def: great respect, or something that makes you proud
examples: It's an honor to meet you, sir.
A dinner was held in honor of the retiring teachers.

senses.def: the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles
examples: He's a man of honor who always keeps his promises.

senses.def: to show great respect for someone, often with a public award or ceremony
examples: The scientist was honored for her work on vaccines.

senses.def: to do what you have promised or agreed to do
examples: The company refused to honor the agreement.

note: American spelling: honor (British: honour). The h is silent: "an honor".

senses.def: a curved piece of metal or plastic used to hang things on or catch fish
examples: Hang your towel on the hook behind the door.
He put a worm on the hook and cast his line.

senses.def: to fasten or hang something using a hook
examples: Hook the trailer to the back of the truck.

senses.def: (hook up/be hooked) to connect a device, or to make someone very interested or addicted
examples: Can you hook up the printer to my laptop?
I watched one episode and now I'm hooked.

note: "Off the hook" = free from blame or a difficult situation. "Hooked on" = addicted to.

senses.def: to want something to happen and think it is possible
examples: I hope you feel better soon.
We're hoping to buy a house next year.

senses.def: the feeling that something good might happen
examples: Doctors say there is still hope for a full recovery.
Never give up hope.

senses.def: a person or thing that may help you get what you want
examples: He's our last hope of winning the game.

note: "I hope so" / "I hope not" are short answers. Use "hope" for possible things and "wish" for unlikely things.

senses.def: believing that something good will happen
examples: Doctors are hopeful that she will make a full recovery.
I'm hopeful we can reach an agreement by Friday.

senses.def: making you believe something good will happen
examples: There are hopeful signs that the economy is recovering.

senses.def: a person who hopes to succeed at something
examples: Dozens of presidential hopefuls attended the debate.

senses.def: used to say what you hope will happen
examples: Hopefully, the rain will stop before the game.
The package should arrive tomorrow, hopefully.

senses.def: in a way that shows hope
examples: The dog looked hopefully at the food on the table.

note: "Hopefully" = Turkish "umarım/inşallah" at the start of a sentence; very common in speech.

senses.def: the line far away where the sky seems to meet the land or sea
examples: We watched the sun sink below the horizon.
A ship appeared on the horizon.

senses.def: (horizons) the limit of your knowledge, experience, or interests
examples: Traveling abroad really broadened my horizons.

note: "On the horizon" = likely to happen soon: More changes are on the horizon.

senses.def: a hard, pointed part that grows on the head of some animals
examples: The bull had long, sharp horns.

senses.def: a device in a vehicle that makes a loud warning sound
examples: The driver behind me kept honking his horn.
Don't blow your horn in a hospital zone.

senses.def: a brass musical instrument that you blow into
examples: She plays the French horn in the school orchestra.

collocations: take the bull by the horns
note: "Take the bull by the horns" = deal with a problem directly. "Lock horns" = argue or fight.

senses.def: very bad or unpleasant
examples: The food at that restaurant was horrible.
I had a horrible dream last night.

senses.def: unkind or mean to people
examples: Why are you being so horrible to your brother?

senses.def: a feeling of great shock and fear
examples: She watched in horror as the car crashed into the wall.
To my horror, I'd left my passport at home.

senses.def: the very unpleasant or terrible nature of something
examples: The book describes the horrors of war.

senses.def: a type of movie or book designed to frighten people
examples: I love watching horror movies on Halloween.

note: "Horror story" can also mean a real bad experience: job-interview horror stories.

senses.def: a large animal with four legs, a mane, and a tail, used for riding and pulling things
examples: She learned to ride a horse when she was ten.
The cart was pulled by two horses.

note: "Straight from the horse's mouth" = directly from the person involved. "Hold your horses" = wait, slow down.

senses.def: a large building where sick or injured people receive medical treatment
examples: He was taken to the hospital after the accident.
She spent three days in the hospital.

note: American English: "in the hospital"; British English: "in hospital" (no article).

senses.def: a person who invites guests and takes care of them
examples: Our host welcomed us with drinks and snacks.
She's a wonderful host — her parties are always fun.

senses.def: a person who presents a TV or radio show
examples: The talk show host interviewed three guests.

senses.def: to organize an event and invite people, or to present a show
examples: Paris hosted the Olympic Games in 2024.
We're hosting a dinner party on Saturday.

senses.def: (a host of) a large number of things or people
examples: The new phone has a host of useful features.

note: "A host of problems/reasons" = many of them.

senses.def: a person who is taken prisoner and may be hurt unless others do what the captors demand
examples: The gunmen took twelve people hostage inside the bank.
All the hostages were released unharmed.

note: Also figurative: "The budget is being held hostage by politics."

senses.def: unfriendly and aggressive, and ready to argue or fight
examples: The crowd became hostile when the police arrived.
He gave me a hostile look.

senses.def: strongly opposed to something
examples: Local residents are hostile to the new airport plan.

senses.def: difficult to live in or succeed in
examples: Few animals can survive in such a hostile environment.

note: American pronunciation /ˈhɑːstl/; British /ˈhɒstaɪl/. "Hostile takeover" = one company buying another against its wishes.

senses.def: unfriendly or aggressive feelings or behavior
examples: There is a lot of hostility between the two neighbors.
The proposal was met with hostility from workers.

senses.def: (hostilities, formal) acts of fighting in a war
examples: Both sides agreed to end hostilities.

senses.def: having a high temperature
examples: It's too hot to go running today.
Be careful, the soup is very hot.

senses.def: having a strong, burning taste
examples: I like my curry really hot.

senses.def: (informal) popular or fashionable, or causing a lot of discussion
examples: Climate change is a hot topic this election year.
That restaurant is the hottest place in town right now.

note: "In hot water" = in trouble. For spicy food, "hot" is common; Turkish "acı" is not "bitter".

senses.def: a building where people pay to stay for a short time
examples: We stayed at a small hotel near the beach.
The hotel has a pool and a gym.

note: Stress is on the second syllable: ho-TEL.

senses.def: a period of 60 minutes
examples: The flight takes about three hours.
I'll be back in an hour.

senses.def: (hours) the time when a business is open or when people work
examples: Our office hours are 9 to 5.
Nurses often work long hours.

note: The h is silent: "an hour". For clock time, say "What time is it?", not "What hour is it?".

senses.def: a building where people live, usually one family
examples: They bought a house with a big backyard.
Let's meet at my house after school.

senses.def: a group that makes laws, or a company or building used for a particular purpose
examples: The bill was passed by the House of Representatives.
She works for a publishing house in New York.

senses.def: to provide a place for people to live, or to contain something
examples: The new building will house 200 students.
The museum houses a famous collection of paintings.

note: Noun /haʊs/, verb /haʊz/. "On the house" = free, paid for by the restaurant or bar.

senses.def: all the people who live together in one house
examples: The average household spends $500 a month on food.
She grew up in a household with five children.

senses.def: connected with a home, or very well known
examples: Keep household chemicals away from children.
The brand became a household name in the 1990s.

note: "A household name" = a person or brand that everyone knows.

senses.def: houses and apartments, especially their type, price, or condition
examples: There's a shortage of affordable housing in the city.
The government promised to build more public housing.

senses.def: a hard cover that protects part of a machine
examples: The engine is inside a metal housing.

note: Uncountable.

senses.def: in what way or by what method
examples: How do you make this sauce?
Can you show me how to use the printer?

senses.def: used to ask about someone's health or the condition of something
examples: How are you today?
How was your trip to Denver?

senses.def: used to ask about amount, age, size, or degree
examples: How much does this jacket cost?
How old is your daughter?

note: "How come?" (informal) = why? "How about…?" makes a suggestion: How about pizza?

senses.def: used to introduce a statement that contrasts with what was said before
examples: The plan sounds good. However, it will be very expensive.
Most people liked the movie; some critics, however, hated it.

senses.tr: ne kadar ... olursa olsun; nasıl ... olursa
senses.def: to whatever degree, or in whatever way
examples: However hard I try, I can't remember his name.
You can decorate the room however you like.

note: Use a period or semicolon before "however" between two clauses, not just a comma. More formal than "but".

senses.def: extremely large in size, amount, or degree
examples: They live in a huge house with eight bedrooms.
The concert was a huge success.

note: "A huge fan of" = someone who likes something very much.

senses.def: relating to people rather than animals, machines, or gods
examples: The accident was caused by human error.
Human rights must be protected.

senses.def: showing the normal feelings and weaknesses of people
examples: Don't worry about the mistake — it's only human.

senses.def: a person, rather than an animal or machine
examples: Dogs can hear sounds that humans cannot.

note: Human = of people; humane = kind, not causing suffering.

senses.def: connected with helping people who are suffering and improving their living conditions
examples: The UN sent humanitarian aid to the earthquake zone.
Aid groups warn of a growing humanitarian crisis.

senses.def: a person who works to improve people's lives
examples: She was a well-known humanitarian who built schools in rural areas.

note: "On humanitarian grounds" = for reasons of kindness and human welfare.

senses.def: all people in the world together
examples: Climate change is one of the greatest threats facing humanity.
The attack was described as a crime against humanity.

senses.def: kindness and understanding toward others
examples: The nurses treated the prisoners with humanity.

senses.def: (the humanities) subjects such as literature, history, and philosophy
examples: She has a degree in the humanities.

senses.def: not thinking you are better or more important than others
examples: Despite his fame, he remained humble and kind.
In my humble opinion, the first version was better.

senses.def: low in social rank or simple and not expensive
examples: She rose from humble beginnings to run a large company.

senses.def: to make someone feel less important or proud
examples: The champions were humbled by a team of amateurs.

senses.def: the quality of being funny, or the ability to laugh at things
examples: She has a great sense of humor.
The speech was full of humor.

senses.def: (formal) the mood someone is in
examples: He was in a good humor all morning.

senses.def: to do what someone wants to keep them happy, even if it seems silly
examples: I didn't believe him, but I humored him and agreed.

note: American spelling: humor (British: humour). Note: humorous has no u in either spelling.

senses.def: funny or showing a sense of humor
examples: He gave a humorous speech at the wedding.
The book takes a humorous look at office life.

note: More formal than "funny".
